mission_config.why: The team's new filter system. All gates, soft weights, bad/good bounds and category tables come from this file.

missions.why: Team lead decision 1 (2026-11-14): exactly three missions are offered, in this order: rover, solar and lunar_base. lunar_base is an exact copy of the thermal block of mission_scoring.json (checked at load time and by a test); thermal and ice stay in that file untouched as components of lunar_base (mission_scoring.json lunar_base.components) and are not offered as missions. The ice component is evaluated on every Earth cell and exported as information only: it never changes the lunar_base ranking. The JSON's own 'offered_missions' list must equal this one.

elevation_m.reason: The common gate elevation_m >= 1 is a land mask written for Earth (its why says 'solo tierra firme, descarta oceano, que el modelo fija en -250 m'). Lunar elevation_m is height relative to a datum (LOLA, 1737.4 km sphere), so on the Moon the same gate would remove 11,041 of 16,200 cells for no physical reason (audit A3 section 2). On the real 1-degree table lunar elevation_m is above the 1737.4 km sphere too and 43,502 of 64,800 lunar cells are below 1 m (real_data/README.md), so the gate stays Earth-only there as well.

mask_fraction.reason: Kept on both bodies exactly as written. On the Moon mask_fraction is the constant 1.0, so the gate never removes a lunar cell. On the real Earth table mask_fraction is the land share of the cell (ESA CCI land cover; inland water counts as water), so the gate means 'at least 30 % land'.

gate_body_applicability.why: Which body each COMMON gate applies to. Thresholds are untouched; only applicability is set here. Mission gates always apply to both bodies. Pending team confirmation.

on_invalid_value.why: A value outside its physically valid range is reported in validity.json and flagged on the cell; it is never clipped, replaced or silently fixed. With today's data no value fails.

value.population: all cells of both bodies that pass the mission's hard filters (concatenated, each cell counted once)

similarity_scale.why: Per-variable physical scale for sim = max(0, 1 - |earth - moon| / scale). A pooled robust physical range keeps real Earth-Moon differences visible: per-body z-scores or percentile ranks would score Earth's largest MODELLED thermal amplitude (38.75 K, formula 8 + 22*bare + 0.0022*elev) as a perfect match for the MODELLED lunar values (63-180 K, formula 180*cos(lat)^0.35). Both ranges are formula output, and the lunar one is contradicted by Diviner (about 250-300 K at low and mid latitudes, R2 section 3; 95-390 K at the equator and about 220 K at polar rims, R3 F10/F12). The population is all passing cells of both bodies concatenated, so the body with more passing cells sets most of the scale (thermal: 16,200 lunar against 2,613 Earth cells); this is pending team confirmation. The rover 'tolerances' in mission_scoring.json are not used as scales because they are defined for 300 m baselines and no table has 300 m values (real 1-degree tables: km-baseline columns; legacy 2-degree table: copies of 2-degree-cell values). USED BY NO SHIPPED RULE: only the physical_pooled similarity rule (--similarity-rule physical_pooled) reads this setting; the shipped rules (rover and solar real_value_tolerance, lunar_base percentile_and_real_tolerance; similarity_rule) use the tolerances of real_value_similarity instead, and the bundle does not export it (statistical audit 2026-11-15, point 9.2.9).

similarity_zero_scale.why: If a pooled range is zero (every passing cell has the same value), sim is 1 when the two values are equal and 0 otherwise, instead of dividing by zero.

mix_factor.why: alpha in mission_scoring.combine_with_similarity: final = alpha * similarity_pct + (1 - alpha) * suitability. 0.5 is that function's own default (mission_scoring.py line 207). Adopting the library default is still a decision on an open question (how much lunar likeness against mission fitness), so it is pending team confirmation; ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3 gives the effect of 0.3 and 0.7 on each mission's top 10.

pairing_chunk_rows.why: Number of Earth cells compared with all candidate lunar cells per vectorised block. Performance and memory only; it does not change results (the twin is an argmax per Earth row). 128 rows x 64,800 lunar cells x 8 bytes = 66 MB per temporary array on the 1-degree grid; 512 needed 265 MB per array.

value.body_rule: weighted mean of level_scores over the mission's weighted variables that have data, using the mission's soft weights
value.pair_rule: min(Earth score, Moon score) * coverage, where coverage = share of the mission's soft weight with data on both cells

confidence.why: Confidence must say how much the numbers behind a ranking can be trusted. A MEASURED value counts fully, a DERIVED one (a stated formula on a measured value) a little less, an UNDOCUMENTED cached array less, and a MODELLED formula least. The weaker body limits the pair. The criteria act at rover-to-site scale, so a cell larger than high_max_cell_km (every 2-degree cell: about 222 km on Earth, about 61 km on the Moon; every 1-degree cell: about 111 km and 30 km) can never be 'high'. A variable counts on a body only where that body's cell has a value; coverage is the share of the soft weight with data on both the Earth cell and its twin. Revision 8 (the team lead's order of 2026-11-15 11:36 CET: remove from the model what carries no information per pair): the label was uniform per mission (every Rover and Solar panels pair 'medium', every Lunar base pair 'low'; 'high' unreachable on 1-degree cells), so export_per_pair is false: the confidence and confidence_score columns of earth_<mission>.bin stay (every value missing, so an older web build reads them and shows no label), and the explain.json fields and missions.json confidence_counts / distributions.confidence_score are gone. Its place is taken by the stability text (top5_stability).

explain_top_n.why: Number of top-ranked Earth cells per mission written with a full per-variable explanation in explain.json; enough for a top-N panel and small on disk.

top_failure_reasons_n.why: Number of commonest failure reasons per mission and body listed in missions.json.

body_radius_km.why: Mean radii used for the true cell size (2*pi*R/180 per 2 degrees) and for great-circle distances. 1737.4 km is the sphere of the LOLA DEM and of the IAU gazetteer .prj; 6371.0 km is the IUGG mean Earth radius.

lunar_gazetteer_csv.why: Offline extract of the USGS/IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (MOON_nomenclature_center_pts, 9,087 features, longitudes 0-360 positive east) made by 'python -m engine gazetteer'. Source file and hash are in engine/data/iau_source.json.

lunar_feature_exclude_types.why: Satellite features are lettered craters named after a parent (e.g. 'Tycho K'); 7,064 of 9,087 entries. Excluding them labels a cell with a primary named feature, which is what a map reader recognises (audit A4 used the same rule for 'nearest primary').

antarctic_label_lat_max.why: reverse_geocoder returns the nearest populated GeoNames place, and there are none in Antarctica, so cells there were labelled 'TF Kerguelen' or 'ZA' (audit A3). Land cells whose centre is at or south of 60 S (the Antarctic Treaty area) are labelled Antarctica (AQ) instead, with no first-level region.

export_decimals.why: Rounding of floats in the bundle. Utilities and per-variable similarities are published with 6 decimals and the engine computes suitability, similarity and the final score from exactly these published values, so the browser reproduces them with the DATA_CONTRACT formulas to about 1e-4 points. Scores are published with 2 decimals and the rank is computed on the published final score (ties by id), so the stored rank follows the contract rule on stored values. Other keys keep the input precision of the CSV (variable values), the IAU gazetteer's precision (iau_lat_lon, diameter_km) and the soft weights (weight). The bundle stays under 12 MB.

mission_titles.why: Short English titles for the app. The team's own descriptions in mission_scoring.json are exported verbatim as 'description'. lunar_base is the lunar base mission whose core is the thermal-endurance configuration.

similarity_comparability.why: A variable that the dataset's registry marks as not the same physical quantity on the two bodies (legacy: provenance.json comparable_across_bodies = false; real tables: datasets.json comparability status 'not_comparable') is left out of the Earth-Moon similarity and of the twin search; it still counts fully in suitability. 'comparable_with_caveat' variables are used and their reason is exported. Comparing bare-ground fraction with a lunar value set by definition, or an Earth air temperature with a lunar surface temperature, would make 'Moon-likeness' measure something else. Pending team confirmation; set false to compare every weighted variable with data on both bodies.

explain_helps_n.why: Number of variables listed in explain.json 'helps_most' (largest final points): enough for a one-line 'why' in the panel.

explain_hurts_n.why: Number of variables listed in explain.json 'hurts_most' (largest lost points above 0).

coordinate_tolerance_deg.why: Largest difference, in degrees, accepted by the schema between a CSV lat/lon and the cell centre computed from row/col. The CSV stores centres with float rounding only; 1e-6 deg is about 0.1 m on Earth.

earth_country_polygons.why: Country of an Earth land cell by point-in-polygon on Natural Earth 1:110m admin-0 countries (public domain). The nearest GeoNames place gave the wrong country for 229 of 5,359 land cells inside a polygon (review). Cells outside every polygon (coasts at 110m resolution, small islands) fall back to the nearest GeoNames place. Source and sha256 in engine/data/ne_source.json.

not_used_by_engine_why.value: tolerances: defined for 300 m baselines, and no table has 300 m values: on the real 1-degree tables the *_300m_* variables are read from km-baseline columns (slope_iso_deg, a slope over about 3.7-3.8 km, and roughness_m, at a lag of about 1.9 km; true_baseline in variables.json), and on the legacy 2-degree table they were copies of 2-degree-cell values. workable_days: not read by mission_scoring.py. domain weights (relieve/material/termico/luz/agua): the team note in mission_scoring.json says they are used only by the web 'Use Weights' button of the similarity; the engine instead weights the similarity with the mission's soft weights, because no mapping from these domains to the new variables exists. This departure is pending team confirmation (ASSUMPTIONS.md section 3).
not_used_by_engine_why.why: Text exported in missions.json 'not_used_by_engine.why' so the app can say why these team settings have no effect.

missing_data_reason.why: A cell whose gated or required variable is empty is eliminated (mission_scoring.json on_missing_gate = 'drop'). The reason code is '<variable>:missing' (as in the v1 bundle and the tests) and the interface label is 'no data: <variable>', so the app can count how many cells each mission loses to missing data (for example Antarctica has no land surface temperature in the real tables).

binary_encoding.why: v2 binary columns: little-endian Float32 (NaN = missing) for cell values and Int32 for everything else, with -2147483648 (INT32_MIN, never a valid value here) as the missing sentinel. Utilities, per-variable similarities, scores and confidence scores are stored as Int32 q with value = q / 10^decimals, using the same decimals as export_decimals, so the browser decodes exactly the published value the engine computed with (a Float32 of 0.123456 is not 0.123456 and would break the exact recompute).

first_view_budget_bytes.why: Size targets of the v2 bundle (2.5 MB = 2,500,000 bytes for manifest, missions, variables, places, Earth base and the default mission; 14 MB = 14,000,000 bytes in total, decimal megabytes so the target holds under either reading), set for loading on a phone. The build reports the sizes and the tests check them; nothing is cut silently to meet them.

similarity_rule.why: Team decision of 2026-11-15 08:55 CET (the team lead's delegate on the team lead's behalf), confirming the recommended design D4b of docs/LUNAR_BASE_PROPOSAL.md: Lunar base uses percentile_and_real_tolerance (real_value_similarity.missions.lunar_base): coldest temperature and daily thermal amplitude compared as mid-rank percentiles within their own population (Earth: the points passing the Lunar base funnel; Moon: the cells of the zone), slope and roughness in real values, pair filter, no twin when no zone cell passes it. Rover and Solar panels keep real_value_tolerance unchanged. Team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning), given by the team lead's delegate on the team lead's behalf, answering docs/ANALOG_PRINCIPLE.md (docs/DECISIONS.md section 'Decisiones tomadas (15-11-2026, mañana)'): the similarity rule is a per-mission setting. Rover and Solar panels use real_value_tolerance (similarity on real values within stated tolerances, real_value_similarity). Lunar base kept zone_twin (z-scores on the nine NASA regions) until 2026-11-15 08:55 CET. Earlier: zone_twin for all three missions (team decision of 2026-11-15, answer 1 to docs/DECISIONS.md), before that repo_global_mean (team lead decision 4, 2026-11-14). A plain string applies one rule to every mission; '--similarity-rule RULE' does that for one build (repo_global_mean, zone_twin and physical_pooled stay available and tested; percentile_and_real_tolerance needs a real_value_similarity block for the mission, so only Lunar base can use it).

value.repo_global_mean: What the repository does by default (analog_finder.compute_analog_ranking with its default target zone 'Global Lunar Surface Mean'): the target is the mean z profile of the whole Moon; one similarity per Earth cell, the same for every mission; no twin. Kept available for comparison; not the shipped rule since 2026-11-15.
value.zone_twin: Used by lunar_base until 2026-11-15 08:55 CET (and by rover and solar until the morning decision of the same day); kept available with --similarity-rule zone_twin: z-score formula of analog_finder against every lunar cell of the mission's zone (similarity_zones); the twin is the single most similar zone cell (ties: lowest id). Lunar cells are not passed through the mission filters.
value.physical_pooled: The integration's earlier rule (engine 1.1-2.0): per-variable sim = max(0, 1 - |earth - moon| / pooled 5-95 percentile range) over the mission's comparable weighted variables, twin among the lunar cells passing the mission. Kept available, not the default.
value.real_value_tolerance: Active for rover and solar since the team decision of 2026-11-15 (morning): per variable a score exp(-0.5 * (|earth - moon| / tolerance)^2) on REAL values (Rover since 11:51 CET: s = 1 within the measurement uncertainty sigma of the elevation models, else exp(-0.5 * max(0, |d| / sigma - 1)^2), sigma 0.265093 deg for slope and 17.4017 m for roughness); similarity = 100 * weighted mean of the scores; pair filter: every key variable within its tolerance and every secondary within twice its tolerance, otherwise no twin; twin = the zone cell passing the filter with the highest similarity (ties: lowest id). Variables, roles, weights, tolerances and zones in real_value_similarity.
value.percentile_and_real_tolerance: Active for lunar_base since the team decision of 2026-11-15 08:55 CET (the team lead's delegate on the team lead's behalf), confirming the recommended design D4b of docs/LUNAR_BASE_PROPOSAL.md: the real_value_tolerance machinery with a scale per variable. Variables with scale 'percentile_within_population' (coldest temperature, daily thermal amplitude) are compared as mid-rank percentiles, 100 * (rank - 0.5) / n with ties averaged, within their own population (Earth: the points that pass the mission's funnel; Moon: the cells of the mission's zone); variables with scale 'real' (slope, roughness) in real values. Per variable s = exp(-0.5 * (difference / tolerance)^2); similarity = 100 * weighted mean; pair filter: key variables within 1 x tolerance, secondary within 2 x tolerance; twin = the zone cell passing the filter with the highest similarity (ties: lowest id); no twin otherwise. It is a likeness of thermal POSITION, not of temperature: the real values and differences are exported per pair.

similarity_rule_options.why: What each value of similarity_rule means; exported in similarity.json so the app can say which rule produced the numbers of each mission.

value.features_and_weights: analog_finder.ANALOG_FEATURES and analog_finder.DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, imported at build time (not copied)

repo_similarity.why: Team lead decision 3: similarity is computed with the repository's own formula. decay 0.45 is the constant of compute_analog_ranking ('similarity_pct = 100.0 * np.exp(-0.45 * rms_dist)'); the Earth population is its land filter ('earth_df["elevation_m"] > 0.0'); the Moon is normalised over all its cells as the function does. zero_variation_threshold is the function's own scale threshold (normalize_planetary_features falls back to the std, then to 1, when a scale is <= 1e-6); it is used only to REPORT variables with zero or near-zero variation on a body (similarity.json variation), never to drop one silently. z-scores are rounded to 4 decimals and similarity_pct to 2 by the function itself (np.round); the bundle stores exactly those published values. A test runs analog_finder.compute_analog_ranking on the legacy table and checks the engine's similarity equals its similarity_pct on every land cell.

lunar_base.name: NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole
lunar_base.source: USGS navigational grids (McClernan 2024, DOI 10.5066/P1MEQ6UK, CC0): each region's footprint is the union of its 1 km grid squares, an upper bound of the region (the exact outline file is not published)

similarity_zones.why: Team lead decision 4 (zone_twin only): rover and solar target the south-pole zone exactly as the code defines it (centre latitude at or below -75). lunar_base targets the lunar cells that intersect NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole (announced 2024-10-28, NASA RELEASE24-136) from the USGS data release (DOI 10.5066/P1MEQ6UK; the exact outlines are not published, so each footprint is the union of the region's 1 km navigational grid squares, an upper bound), if a verified region file is present in the repository (engine/data/artemis_iii_regions.geojson: GeoJSON in planetocentric degrees, longitude -180..180 east-positive, top-level 'verified': true, copied from the proposal agent's verified outlines); otherwise the south-pole zone (never the global mean). The zone used and the reason are written to similarity.json. Lunar cells are not passed through the mission filters. Confirmed by the team on 2026-11-15 (rover and solar stay on the south-pole zone, the branch's version from analog_finder.py commit ff6f1ae, not Tycho; lunar_base on the nine NASA regions).

twin_tie_rule.why: zone_twin: when two zone cells are at exactly the same distance (double precision) from an Earth cell, the one with the lowest lunar cell id is the twin, so the result does not depend on processing order.

detail_tile_rows.why: Per-cell funnel detail (utilities, z-scores, the ice component) is split into files of this many grid rows (18 files on the 180-row grid), so the app loads about one eighteenth of the detail to show any land cell instead of every mission file. Layout only; no effect on results.

similarity_meaning.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the single 1-degree lunar cell, inside the mission's target zone, that holds the most similar relative position on the Moon as the Earth point holds on Earth (slope, roughness, relative elevation and surface temperature, each compared within its own world). A high similarity means 'same place in each world's range', not 'same values': both sets of values are shown side by side.
similarity_meaning.where: nowhere in the shipped bundle (no longer applies: it described the z-score rule (zone_twin) that Lunar base used until 2026-11-15 08:55 CET; Lunar base now uses percentile_and_real_tolerance (texts similarity_meaning_lunar_base, lunar_base_pair_sentence)); kept for the --similarity-rule zone_twin and repo_global_mean builds
similarity_meaning.status: no longer applies: it described the z-score rule (zone_twin) that Lunar base used until 2026-11-15 08:55 CET; Lunar base now uses percentile_and_real_tolerance (texts similarity_meaning_lunar_base, lunar_base_pair_sentence)

similarity_meaning_real_values.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the 1-degree lunar cell, inside the mission's target zone, whose real values are closest. Similarity is computed on real values within stated tolerances: every key variable of the twin is within its tolerance of the Earth point and every secondary variable within twice its tolerance, and each variable scores lower the further apart the two values are. Each mission has its own score rule. Solar panels: the score falls from 1 with the first difference, as exp(-0.5 (difference / tolerance)^2). Rover: a difference within the measurement uncertainty of the elevation models (slope 0.27 degrees, roughness 17.4 m) scores 1, and beyond it the score falls as exp(-0.5 max(0, difference / uncertainty - 1)^2). Both values and their difference are shown side by side.
similarity_meaning_real_values.where: rover and solar (real_value_tolerance rule): wherever a similarity is shown, next to each similarity variable's Earth value, lunar value, difference and tolerance (earth_<mission>_pairs.bin '<variable>.earth', '<variable>.moon', '<variable>.diff'; tolerances in missions.json similarity.variables)

similarity_meaning_lunar_base.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the 1-degree cell, among NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole, that holds the same thermal position and has a similar terrain. The coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as positions: where the point ranks among Earth's lunar-base candidates against where its twin ranks among the cells of the nine regions, each within 10 percentile points; the two places are not equally cold and the real values are far apart. Slope and roughness are compared in real values (the twin within 4 degrees and 60 m). The real values on both sides and their differences are shown next to every pair.
similarity_meaning_lunar_base.where: lunar_base (percentile_and_real_tolerance rule): wherever a similarity is shown, next to each variable's percentile on both sides (earth_lunar_base_pairs.bin '<variable>.earth_pct', '.moon_pct', '.diff_pct') and the real values and differences ('<variable>.earth', '.moon', '.diff', 'info.<variable>.*')

lunar_base_swing_gate.text: The Lunar base keeps the team's gate 'daily thermal swing at least {gate_min} K'. Without it, Earth cells with a swing of about 1 K (for example on Ellesmere Island) would match the Moon's coldest temperature at a similarity of about 99, and the key variable, the thermal swing, would carry no weight in practice. The recognised polar stations therefore do not pass: daily land-surface swing {sites}; McMurdo and Concordia have no land-surface temperature in the table. They are analogs of cold and isolation, not of thermal cycling.

lunar_base_criteria.decision: 2026-11-15 11:28, 11:36 and 11:51 CET (the team lead, through his delegate; docs/DECISIONS.md 'Decisiones de las 11:28 y 11:36')
lunar_base_criteria.text: The Lunar base suitability uses one criterion for the ground instead of two: the bare-or-sparse fraction (from ESA CCI land cover, continuous, without the urban class) weighs 25 %; the thermal-inertia class (built from the same land-cover classes) and the permafrost class (modelled, missing on 607 of 2,419 passing points, with no sourced link to a base) carry no weight. The thermal-inertia class is still required and still excludes water. The four weights left (daily temperature swing 35 %, coldest temperature 25 %, bare-or-sparse fraction 25 %, ground sunlight 10 %) sum to 95 %, and the suitability is divided by that sum, so in effect they weigh 36.8 %, 26.3 %, 26.3 % and 10.5 %.

constants_two_values.text: Two constants appear with two values. Earth's radius: the engine uses 6,371.0 km (for distances, cell sizes and the 2-degree separation); the Earth-table builder used 6,371.0088 km for its relief metrics. The 2-degree arc is 222.390 km with 6,371.0 and 222.390 km with 6,371.0088 (0.3 m apart; 222.4 km at the published precision). Over the 180 latitudes the sunlight above the atmosphere differs by at most 0.00012 kWh per square metre per day (it moves the 4th published decimal on 68 latitudes, never the 3rd); no number entering a result was changed.
